newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW -- Multifoods CEO sees division growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW -- Multifoods CEO sees division growth.

text.p: The new chairman of International Multifoods Corp said Monday he sees growth opportunities in each of the company's businesses to improve overall results at the Minneapolis-based firm.

"There are strengths in every one of (Multifoods') businesses that we can capitalize on," said Gary Costley, a former Kellogg Co executive who was named chairman, chief executive and president of Multifoods.
Multifoods, whose former chairman resigned in May, has been trying to turn around its business segments, especially vending distribution.

Multifoods said in September that its full-year earnings are likely to be less than last year due to problems in its vending distribution business. Significant progress had been made in the remainder of the distribution businesses, Venezuela Foods and the bakery segments, the company added at the time.
The company earned $1.31 a share before unusual items in fiscal 1996 ended in February versus $1.55 the year before.
The main priority for Costley will be to devise a strategic plan for Multifoods, including taking a hard look at various divisions, Piper Jaffray analyst George Dahlman said.
"It's not going to be an easy task," Dahlman said. "But it's far too early to make any prognostication where the company is going to go," he added.
Costley declined to say what steps he might take at the helm of Mulitfoods. "I can't speculate on what strategy shifts might come out...," he added in a telephone interview.
Costly replaces Robert Price, who had been chairman and chief executive officer on an interim basis, following the resignation in May of Anthony Luiso. Price remains a board member.

Costley, 53, spent 24 years at Kellogg, including as executive vice president and area director of Kellogg North America. He said he left Kellogg to start his search for a chief executive job, which had been a long-time career goal.
In the interim, he was dean of the Babcock Graduate School of Management at Wake Forest University.
